skills.trigger: When evaluating asymmetric diaphragmatic contours on a chest X-ray to distinguish pathological elevation from normal anatomical variants.
steps: Compare the height and contour of both hemidiaphragms; identify if one side is significantly elevated with a smooth, continuous dome shape while the other exhibits scalloping or undulation.

Associate marked, smooth elevation (especially on the right) with diaphragmatic paralysis or phrenic nerve palsy, whereas recognize scalloped or wavy contours (often on the left) as a benign anatomical variant like eventration rather than acute pathology.
